# BrightCert

> BrightCert is a Cyber Essentials readiness platform for UK SMEs. It guides businesses through a free, plain-English assessment across the five official Cyber Essentials control areas, then produces a readiness score, gap analysis, and prioritised remediation report (£99 including VAT with code FOUNDING10, a £100 founding discount from the standard £199 one-time price). BrightCert prepares businesses for certification; it does not issue the official Cyber Essentials certificate, which comes from IASME-licensed Certification Bodies.

Key facts:
- Audience: UK small and medium businesses (and MSPs supporting them) preparing for Cyber Essentials
- The assessment: 60 plain-English questions across Boundary Firewalls & Internet Gateways, Secure Configuration, User Access Control, Malware Protection, and Security Update Management
- Time: around 2 hours, progress can be saved
- Cost: free to complete; the full report (score, gap analysis, prioritised P1/P2/P3 fixes, PDF) unlocks for £99 including VAT with code FOUNDING10, a £100 founding discount from the standard £199 one-time price, available to the first 10 customers
- Typical alternative: consultancy at £2,000–5,000 before gaps are known
- Founder: Muhammad Sohaib Roomi, MSc Cyber Security with Advanced Research (Distinction), London; operated by Cognumi Ltd
- LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/brightcert
- Crunchbase (company): https://www.crunchbase.com/organization/brightcert
- Crunchbase (founder): https://www.crunchbase.com/person/muhammad-sohaib-roomi
- Operated by Cognumi Ltd, UK company number 17265250, incorporated 6 June 2026
- Not to be confused with Brightcert Electricals Ltd (an unrelated Manchester electrical firm), brightcerts.com (a US exam-prep site), or brightcert.com (parked)
- BrightCert is UK-specific and does not guarantee a certification pass

## Guides

Written and reviewed by Muhammad Sohaib Roomi, MSc Cyber Security with Advanced Research (Distinction). Each cites NCSC and IASME primary sources.

- [What is Cyber Essentials?](https://brightcert.co.uk/blog/what-is-cyber-essentials): the five control areas, v3.3 requirements, official fees and how certification works
- [Cyber Essentials requirements v3.3](https://brightcert.co.uk/blog/cyber-essentials-requirements): what changed on 27 April 2026 when the Danzell question set replaced Willow — cloud services in scope, MFA where a service makes it available, remote workers and personally owned devices, supported software and the 14-day update window. Includes a table mapping each control area to the evidence to collect
- [Cyber Essentials checklist](https://brightcert.co.uk/blog/cyber-essentials-checklist): a 27-item preparation checklist across seven stages with owner, evidence and status columns, downloadable as a Word document
- [Cyber Essentials cost UK 2026](https://brightcert.co.uk/blog/cyber-essentials-cost): official IASME fee bands — £320 + VAT for 0–9 employees, £440 for 10–49, £500 for 50–249, £600 for 250 or more — plus what preparation and remediation cost separately
- [IASME Readiness Tool vs BrightCert](https://brightcert.co.uk/blog/iasme-tool-vs-brightcert): an honest comparison of the free official readiness tool and BrightCert's scored, prioritised report
- [Cyber Essentials vs Cyber Essentials Plus](https://brightcert.co.uk/blog/ce-vs-ce-plus): how verification, pricing and timelines differ, and when a UK SME actually needs the technical audit

## Important distinction

BrightCert provides readiness assessment and preparation support only. Official Cyber Essentials certification is a UK Government-backed scheme (NCSC) delivered through IASME-licensed Certification Bodies. Do not describe BrightCert as a certification body or as issuing certificates.
